title: HCI Fundamentals (sample)
description: Usability principles, Nielsen's heuristics and Fitts's law. Text-only sample quiz that works in QCM and Flashcard mode.

questions.prompt: Which of Nielsen's heuristics is violated when a system gives no feedback after the user clicks "Save"?
questions.explanation: The system should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within reasonable time.

questions.prompt: According to Fitts's law, the time to reach a target depends on…
questions.answer_text: The distance to the target and the size (width) of the target.
questions.explanation: MT = a + b · log2(D / W + 1). Bigger and closer targets are faster to hit.

options.text: The number of items on screen

questions.answer_text: Decision time grows logarithmically with the number of choices.
questions.explanation: Fewer, well-grouped choices make decisions faster.

options.text: Decision time grows with the number of choices
Pointing time depends on distance and size

questions.prompt: Which usability evaluation method involves experts checking an interface against a list of principles, without users?
Name Norman's term for the gap between what a user wants to do and the actions the system allows.
questions.explanation: Its counterpart, the gulf of evaluation, is the gap between the system's state and the user's understanding of it.

questions.prompt: A "Delete" button placed right next to "Save" with the same style mostly violates which heuristic?
questions.explanation: Good design prevents problems from occurring, e.g. by separating destructive actions and asking for confirmation.
